title: Granular request-quality contracts, banked error budgets, and progressive circuit-fallback protocol
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Define and onboard a set of per-endpoint and per-model request-quality contracts (SLI/SLO), plus an operational policy for banked error budgets, progressive circuit breakers, and automated cross-region credit borrowing. This ticket produces the canonical SLI names, measurement queries, acceptance criteria, simulation plan, and a lightweight runbook for automated actions when budgets are burning fast. Goal: enable deterministic failover and graceful degradation without manual intervention for customer-facing inference routes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canonical SLI/SLO table finalized and reviewed by Reliability, Product, and Support. 2) Telemetry queries (PromQL/ClickHouse) for each SLI validated against 30 days of historical traffic and stored in metrics repo. 3) Simulation harness (traffic replay + injected latency/errors) demonstrates expected automated actions for three scenarios: gradual burn, sudden spike, region outage. 4) Runbook and automation playbook checked into ops repo and a tabletop exercised with SREs. 5) Demo of cross-region borrow/repay with credit decay policy in staging.
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Reliability, Product, and Console teams. Agreed on scope: per-route generation endpoints, chat sessions, and embeddings endpoints first wave.
2026-02-20: Drafted canonical SLI names and initial measurement windows. Circulated to stakeholders: reliability@, pm@, support@.
2026-02-24: Telemetry engineer validated p50/p95/p99 latency buckets and tokenized success/failure events in ClickHouse; found missing flags for partial-responses; added event generation PR.
2026-02-28: First simulation run in staging: heavy tail exhibited when KV-cache miss rate > 30%. Determined cache-aware shedding threshold is needed.
2026-03-02: Design review with Console team passed; added a canary gating requirement for rollout of circuit-breaker automations.
proposed_metrics_queries: tail_latency_p99_9_per_route: quantile(0.999, request_latencies_ms) grouped by route, model_variant over 10m
model_quality_regression: 1 - (f1_score_recent / f1_score_baseline) measured per promptset daily
circuit_and_shedding_policy: Phase 0 (observe): burn_rate < 0.5x -> no action; emit alert to channel #slo-alerts
Phase 1 (soft-throttle): 0.5x <= burn_rate < 2x -> reduce per-tenant concurrency by 10% for low-priority routes and enable prefix caching where available

Phase 2 (progressive-shed): 2x <= burn_rate < 10x -> enable route-level queueing with length cap, reject new lower-priority requests with well-formed 429+Retry-After and hint header 'x-rw-shed-reason', route traffic to compatible quantized model variants for non-critical routes

Phase 3 (circuit open): burn_rate >= 10x or persistent p99.9 latency > SLO for 5m -> open circuit for low-priority model variants, enable cross-region borrow (if credits available), start automated regional fallback to reserve capacity with degraded model variant
Phase 4 (regional ejection): if region health < 70% and borrow unsuccessful -> mark region read-only and divert new sessions to healthy regions with sticky fallthrough policy
banking_and_credit_policy: Each endpoint accrues error-budget credit when under-utilizing its declared SLO; credits are tokenized daily and capped at 14 days of accrual.

Cross-region borrowing: destination region may borrow up to 20% of another region's banked credits if lender region's remaining credits > 30% of its nominal budget; borrow action creates repay obligation with exponential decay within 48h.
Credit expiry: unused credits older than 14 days are expired to prevent unbounded accumulation.
Manual override: Platform SREs can grant emergency one-time credits via console with an audit event recorded.
Accounting: all borrow/repay events logged to metrics and to the billing ledger for postmortem analysis.
simulation_plan: Traffic replay from two representative tenants across chat and generation routes with increasing QPS ramps.
Inject KV-cache cold starts and 5s tail latency events at 1% and 10% intensities.
Simulate region outage by dropping 30% of capacity and ensure borrow/repay flows run and region ejection triggers after thresholds.
Verify circuit transitions and emitted telemetry (alerts, shed events, retry headers) and evaluate customer-visible error surfaces.
Record and analyze cost impact when switching to quantized variants during Phase 2/3.
runbook_steps: 1) On SLO alert: review burn-rate dashboard and SLI trends; confirm simulation vs live anomaly.
2) If Phase 1: notify product owners and enable soft-throttle policy; observe 15m for stabilization.
3) If Phase 2: enable progressive-shed policy via automation; update on-call channel and activate customer notification template for high-risk tenants.
4) If Phase 3: initiate cross-region borrow; begin automated routing to reserve quantized variants; open incident if borrow fails.
5) Post-incident: capture borrow/repay ledger, annotate runbook with lessons, consider SLO adjustment or capacity reservation proposals.
notes: Key trade-offs discussed in design review: (1) how aggressive to make the borrow policy without destabilizing lender regions, (2) visibility vs noise when emitting 429s to customers, (3) preference to prefer quantized variants only for stateless generation routes to avoid loss of conversational context. Next steps: finalize measurement queries, complete the telemetry PR, and run full simulation in staging by 2026-03-12.
